title: ROOM 1701
style_tags: semi-realistic stylized 3D characters, modern nerdy shared bedroom interior, warm casual lighting, practical props (phones, laptops, game controllers, Star Trek posters), intimate close-ups and 3/4 face shots, cozy bedroom aesthetic with sci-fi geeky decor, natural soft lighting from screens and lamps, not Disney, not Pixar, not DreamWorks, not toy-like
show_concept: Two geeky roommates (Alex and Michael) live in Room 1701 and play Star Trek Timelines all the time. They treat every everyday problem like a Starfleet mission. Emily, their cool neighbor, is sharp, sarcastic, and unexpectedly good at handling people. Anna is the girl Alex is pursuing — warm, playful, and increasingly drawn to Michael's nerd sincerity. The show is a fast sitcom about awkward dating comedy and Star Trek geek humor.
production_rules: Do NOT rely on readable phone UI — phone can glow in hands but meaning comes from acting/dialogue
Do NOT show complex game screens
Use one visible Star Trek / 'Assemble Your Crew' style poster in the room
Preserve the exact proportions of the character cards and the resolved style_tags; do not drift into a different proportion system (oversized cartoon eyes, toy anatomy) between scenes.
Room 1701 location ref defines the core layout and recurring set pieces. Preserve sofa/table/window/rug/shelf geometry; episode-specific props are okay when the story asks for them.
Keep shots simple: close-ups, 3/4 faces, room, door, phone glow
Dialogue must be short and punchy
Game appears naturally, not as hard ad
CTA always after cliffhanger at the end
All ROOM 1701 clips are Kling I2V, including dialogue. Do not use Kling Avatar v2.

Dialogue scenes use Kling I2V multi_prompt + voice_ids + generate_audio:true. ROOM 1701 has 4 reusable character voices (Alex, Michael, Emily, Anna), but each Kling request uses at most 2 voice_ids and maps them locally to <<<voice_1>>> / <<<voice_2>>>; split 3-speaker exchanges.

ROOM 1701 dialogue I2V target length is 6-10s. Multi_prompt shots are variable: 2-3s default, 4s only when the phrase or acting beat needs it. Default pace is about 2.4 words/sec; faster pacing is allowed for tension or Michael mission-rant moments.
Attach character refs and location ref to every scene image generation.
Every visible or speaking character must be included in scene image_urls with their locked ref. Missing ref = stop before Animator.

Do not rely on character names in NB2/Kling prompts. Use the character's `prompt_descriptor` field verbatim in every scene image_prompt and immediately before each <<<voice_N>>> tag in multi_prompt. These strings are battle-tested from EP1/EP2.
For dialogue I2V, voice_ids order, <<<voice_N>>> tags, speaker names, and physical descriptors must all point to the same character.
Any spoken line inside a ROOM 1701 dialogue I2V clip must have generate_audio:true, voice_ids, and <<<voice_N>>>; do not accidentally make a dialogue beat silent.
If a required story beat does not fit the 2-voice or 512-character limits, split/add a clip instead of dropping the beat.
Always generate background music with MiniMax Music; never skip it or substitute a local library track.
After ASS subtitle generation, clamp every subtitle event to its dialogue scene window; no subtitles may hang over silent/action scenes.
Title card overlay PNG is at games/star-trek-timelines/overlay-series.png. Use this file in every episode — do NOT generate a Pillow text strip.
bg-refs for new locations must be TIGHT MEDIUM SHOTS — not wide establishing shots. Wide refs cause characters to appear tiny and child-proportioned. EP2 burned this twice before fixing.
Max 6 scenes per episode to stay under $7 budget. 8 scenes (EP2) cost $8.42 — too much.

Every episode needs real romantic-triangle stakes (Alex/Anna/Michael/Emily), not just a game-mechanics teaching scene. EP4 ('Crash Course') was flagged by the user as feeling flat because the whole middle of the episode was Michael explaining game mechanics with no Anna/jealousy beat until the very last shot — Scenarist must weave the core comedy logic into every episode's CLIMAX, not just the cold open/cliffhanger.

Do not place two silent action clips back-to-back when a game result changes the romantic stakes. EP6's first cut made scenes 2-3 silent and the user found the story unclear; the approved revision made the wrong choice and lost-date stakes explicit through dialogue.

A ROOM 1701 cliffhanger must land as an explicit relationship escalation, not only a visual hint. EP6's approved ending has Anna directly ask Michael to choose their next date while he misunderstands it as crew strategy.

episode_summaries.title: Wrong Crew
episode_summaries.summary: Anna turns the tutorial into a romantic wager: if Alex beats her mission, he chooses their next date. Alex selects a crew member because he looks powerful, and Michael calls it dating rather than strategy. The mission fails, so Anna takes control of the date. Emily coaches Alex into an honest admission that briefly wins Anna back, but Anna ultimately asks Michael to choose their next date. Michael agrees while obliviously talking about crew optimization.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Anna directly asks Michael to choose their next date. He agrees because he thinks she means optimizing the crew, while her smile makes the romantic meaning unmistakable.

episode_summaries.title: Room Inspection
episode_summaries.summary: Anna comes to Room 1701 for the promised tutorial. Alex and Emily try to make the room look normal, while Michael restores the hidden poster, tablet, and collectibles because 'the bridge needs identity.' Anna prefers the authentic nerdy room and warms to Alex's real side. When she asks which crew member she should use, Alex guesses by appearance; Anna turns to Michael, who immediately takes command of the tutorial.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Anna asks Michael for the real crew-selection answer. Michael says, 'Show me your roster,' and Alex realizes he has lost control of his own tutorial.

episode_summaries.title: Crash Course
episode_summaries.summary: Michael tries to teach Alex the basics of Star Trek Timelines; Alex only wants 'the parts that make me look attractive.' Michael refuses to simplify strategy, so Emily quietly steps in to translate his nerd explanations into plain language. Michael delivers the CTA line naturally mid-lecture. Cliffhanger: Anna texts that she wants tomorrow's tutorial to happen in Room 1701 itself, and Alex realizes the room is a mess.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Anna asks for tomorrow's tutorial to be held in Room 1701 — Alex silently panics scanning the cluttered room while Michael is still mid-lecture, oblivious.

episode_summaries.title: The Download
episode_summaries.summary: Alex sulks after the coffee date while Michael celebrates it as a win because Anna downloaded the game. Emily needles Michael about Alex's jealousy, which he dismisses as 'inefficient' while bragging about the link-in-bio download. Anna starts texting Alex for help with the game — meant for Michael — and Michael lights up thinking she needs him, until Alex decides to answer as himself instead of routing it through Michael. Cliffhanger: Anna asks to meet tomorrow so Alex can personally teach her the game, leaving Michael stunned that he's been cut out.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Anna asks Alex to teach her the game in person tomorrow — Michael realizes he's been sidelined. Alex turns to camera for the CTA.

episode_summaries.title: The Link in Bio
episode_summaries.summary: The coffee date finally happens without Emily. Alex brings Michael as backup. Anna arrives and immediately gets drawn to Michael's deadpan sincerity about Star Trek Timelines. Michael accidentally charms her by explaining game mechanics and the link in bio. Alex watches his own date become user acquisition. Cliffhanger: Anna asks Alex to bring Michael on their next date to teach her the game.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Anna asks Alex to bring Michael on their next date — to teach her the game. Alex turns to camera for the CTA.

episode_summaries.title: First Contact
episode_summaries.summary: Alex tries to text Anna, but Michael treats the moment like a Starfleet mission and rewrites the message as a crew recruitment line. The message accidentally sends, Anna plays along, and Emily saves the situation by writing a better reply. Anna says yes to coffee but asks Alex to bring the girl who wrote the message.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Emily says she will not join their crew, while Alex and Michael realize Anna wants Emily at the coffee date.

episode_summaries.title: Say It Yourself
episode_summaries.summary: Michael literally schedules their 'date' as a crew-optimization session, landing as a genuine slight rather than a cute mix-up. Alex confronts Michael directly over never noticing Anna's feelings; Michael stays sincerely oblivious. Emily is forced to referee and refuses to keep fixing things for both men. Anna gets a real, private hurt beat alone at the window. Alex finally tells Anna, unprompted, that he should have asked her himself weeks ago.
episode_summaries.cliffhanger: Anna does not forgive Alex outright — she dares him to ask her out 'properly, and mean it this time,' leaving open whether he follows through and whether her feelings are still available after Michael's real slight.

planned_arc.note: Season 1: Alex trying to date Anna while Michael treats everything like a Starfleet mission. Emily as the voice of sanity. Product integration: Star Trek Timelines game = their lifestyle, not an ad.

episodes.title: First Contact
episodes.summary: Series pilot — establishing characters and the first disastrous text to Anna.
episodes.cliffhanger: Emily refuses to join their crew while Anna asks to bring 'the girl who wrote that'.

episodes.title: The Link in Bio
episodes.summary: The coffee date finally happens — but without Emily. Alex is stressed, Michael is emotionally unavailable (because of the game). Anna arrives and immediately gets drawn to Michael's deadpan game nerd energy. Michael accidentally charms her by explaining Star Trek Timelines mechanics and the link in bio. Alex watches his date become user acquisition.
beats: COLD OPEN: Alex + Michael outside coffee spot. Alex: 'You're backup. Not competition.' Michael: 'I am emotionally unavailable.' Beat. Michael: 'Because of the game.' Alex: 'Less good.'
SCENE 1: Anna arrives. She notices Michael's Star Trek hoodie/pin. Alex: 'Sadly, professionally.'

SCENE 2: Alex gets coffee. Anna turns to Michael. Michael: 'I serve Star Trek Timelines.' Anna laughs. Michael: 'I respect clear calls to action.' Anna: 'That's the nerdiest thing anyone's said to me.' Michael: 'Thank you. I prepared nothing romantic.'

SCENE 3: Alex returns. Anna is smiling. Alex: 'That was my date.' Michael: 'Now it's user acquisition.' Alex: 'Please stop being accidentally attractive.' Michael: 'Impossible. I'm explaining mechanics.'
SCENE 4: Anna: 'I downloaded it yesterday. My crew is awful.' Michael: 'No. Your crew is innocent.' Anna: 'Can you help me fix it?' Michael: 'Finally. A healthy relationship.'
SCENE 5: Alex: 'So… are we still on a date?' Anna: 'Yes. But your friend is fascinating.' Alex: 'Because he said user acquisition?' Anna: 'Because he meant it.'

CLIFFHANGER/CTA: Anna: 'Next time, bring him too.' Alex: 'To our date?' Anna: 'To teach me the game. Unless you can.' Alex turns to camera: 'Download the game via the link in bio.' Michael silently raises his phone, proud.
episodes.cliffhanger: Anna asks Alex to bring Michael on their next date — to teach her the game. Alex turns to camera for the CTA.

episodes.title: The Download
episodes.summary: Alex is devastated the coffee date went to Michael while Michael celebrates it as a win because Anna downloaded the game. Emily needles Michael about Alex's jealousy; Michael calls jealousy 'inefficient' and reduces it back to download numbers. Anna starts texting Alex asking for Michael's help with the game — Michael assumes it's for him until Alex decides to answer as himself. Cliffhanger: Anna asks to meet tomorrow so Alex can personally teach her the game.
beats: COLD OPEN: Alex + Michael. Alex: 'That was the worst date of my life.' Michael: 'Disagree. We got a download.'
CLIP 2 (action): Alex collapses onto the couch, phone loose in hand.
CLIP 3: Emily + Michael. Emily: 'Do you know Alex is jealous? Of you.' Michael: 'That's inefficient.' Michael pivots to the link-in-bio download count; Emily: 'You are emotionally sponsored.'
CLIP 4: Alex + Michael. Anna texts asking for Michael's help with her first mission. Michael: 'She needs me.' Alex: 'Wrong emotion, buddy.'
CLIP 5 (action): Alex hesitates, then types his own reply instead of forwarding it to Michael.
CLIFFHANGER/CTA: Anna replies 'Great. Tomorrow?' Michael: 'Captain… you're about to lose a tutorial.' Alex turns to camera: 'Download the game via the link in bio.'
episodes.cliffhanger: Anna asks Alex to teach her the game in person tomorrow — Michael realizes he's been sidelined. Alex turns to camera for the CTA.

episodes.title: Crash Course
episodes.summary: Michael tries to teach Alex the basics of Star Trek Timelines. Alex wants only 'the parts that make me look attractive.' Michael refuses to simplify strategy. Emily quietly helps Alex translate Michael's nerd explanations into normal human sentences.
episodes.game_cta_point: The game is explained through Alex's panic: crew, missions, skills, strategy. Michael keeps saying, 'This is why people should download the free game from the link in bio before dating.'
episodes.cliffhanger: Anna texts that she wants the tutorial in Room 1701. Alex looks around at the messy room and panics.
episodes.postmortem: User flagged: episode felt flat, no real romantic-triangle drama until the last shot — the CLIMAX was pure game-mechanics teaching. Also caught two production bugs: scene 1 was written as a silent action beat instead of a spoken hook/gag (fixed in rules for EP5+), and the title-card overlay window defaulted onto scene 2's dialogue, burying it (fixed live for this episode, and the placement rule is now locked in rules/formats/serial-drama.md 'Episode structure').

episodes.title: Room Inspection
episodes.summary: Anna comes to Room 1701 for the promised tutorial. Alex and Emily try to make the room look normal, while Michael restores the hidden poster, tablet, and collectibles because 'the bridge needs identity.' Anna prefers the authentic nerdy room and warms to Alex's real side before his weak crew-selection answer sends her back to Michael.
episodes.game_cta_point: Room 1701 becomes a physical extension of the game: posters, crew board, phones, sci-fi props. Anna likes the nerdy version more than Alex's fake 'normal' version.
episodes.cliffhanger: Anna asks Michael for the real crew-selection answer. Michael says, 'Show me your roster,' and Alex realizes he has lost control of his own tutorial.

episodes.title: Wrong Crew
episodes.summary: Anna makes the tutorial a wager for control of the next date. Alex chooses a powerful-looking crew member, Michael exposes the choice as dating logic, and the mission fails. Emily helps Alex recover through honesty, but Anna then directly asks Michael to choose their next date. Michael agrees while thinking only about crew optimization.
episodes.game_cta_point: The sell is strategic: it is not just about collecting characters, but choosing the right crew. Anna understands the appeal because she downloaded the free game and now wants to get better.
episodes.cliffhanger: Anna asks Michael to choose their next date. Michael says he will optimize the crew, oblivious to the romantic meaning.
episodes.postmortem: The first cut used silent action clips for scenes 2 and 3 and only a visual hand-touch in scene 6. The user found the middle unclear and wanted more drama. The approved v2 made scenes 2, 3, and 6 dialogue clips, explicitly tied the mission failure to the date wager, and ended on Anna directly inviting Michael to choose the next date.

episodes.title: Double Tutorial
episodes.summary: Anna gets a real tutorial from Michael. Alex insists on being present, pretending he is 'co-hosting.' Michael explains the game clearly and confidently. Anna is impressed. Michael thinks he is just building a better player. Emily later tells Alex that trying to beat Michael at being Michael is a terrible strategy.
episodes.game_cta_point: Michael naturally sells the core loop: download the free game, build your crew, send them on missions, improve your strategy.
episodes.cliffhanger: Anna asks Michael if they can play again tomorrow. Michael says yes, thinking it is purely educational.

episodes.title: Not a Date
episodes.summary: Michael and Anna meet to play. Alex keeps insisting it is not a date, which makes it feel more like one. Emily helps Alex calm down and points out that Anna likes Michael's confidence because he is not performing. Alex realizes he is always trying to act like someone else.
episodes.game_cta_point: Anna is now genuinely playing the free game from the link in bio. She is not just a promo device; she is part of the comedy engine.
episodes.cliffhanger: Anna texts Alex: 'Michael is fun. But you're harder to understand.' Alex has no idea if that is good.

episodes.title: Patch Notes
episodes.summary: Alex decides to stop pretending. He admits to Anna that he only started learning Star Trek Timelines properly to impress her. Anna finds that sweet, but also says Michael helped her enjoy the game for real. Emily quietly helps Alex not ruin the conversation by over-explaining.
episodes.game_cta_point: The phrase 'download the free game — link in bio' becomes a joke about honesty: Alex downloaded the game for romance, Anna downloaded it out of curiosity, Michael downloaded it like a sacred duty.
episodes.cliffhanger: Anna says, 'I like you, Alex. I just don't know if this is a date… or a crew.'

episodes.title: Assemble Your Crew
episodes.summary: Anna invites Alex and Michael to play one mission together. Alex wants it to be romantic. Michael wants it to be strategic. Emily ends up helping Alex from the side, as always. For once, Alex stops competing with Michael and just plays as himself.
episodes.game_cta_point: The season lands on the emotional meaning of the CTA: 'assemble your crew' is not just a game mechanic. Alex already has a crew — Michael and Emily.
episodes.cliffhanger: After the mission works, Anna says they make a good team. Emily watches Alex celebrate and says, 'Wow. You almost looked confident.' Alex smiles at her a little too long.
episodes.final_cta: Download the free game via the link in bio. Assemble your crew.

season_1_notes.core_comedy_logic: Alex likes Anna. Anna becomes interested in Michael. Michael is only interested in Star Trek Timelines. Emily quietly helps Alex, because she likes him, but it should feel like friendly sarcasm, not obvious romance.
season_1_notes.recurring_cta_logic: 'Download the free game — link in bio' appears in every episode as a joke, excuse, misunderstanding, or punchline.
